source_title: New real-time data marks waste burning as one of top sources of air pollution - The Times of India
source_excerpt: New Delhi: Waste burning has now become one of the top sources of Delhiâs air pollution. Between Oct 22 and 26, the daily contribution of waste burning was less than 5%, but its daily share rose significantly in the past two days. It is expected to rise further during the winter months.Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorologyâs new laboratory, Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory, was inaugurated on Oct 24 at New Rajendra Nagar and provides real-time source apportionment data.Burning of garbage, wood, and garden and plastic waste is one of the major sources of pollution in Delhi in winter. Segregation and decentralised composting should be enforced, starting with bulk generators.âDahiya added that open burning must be penalised year-round, not only under Graded Response Action Plan, and National Clean Air Programme funds must be tied to measurable cuts in burning incidents.Anumita Roychowdhury, executive director of research and advocacy at Centre for Science and Environment, said Delhiâs waste burning reflected inadequate efforts to fulfil Swachh Bharat Mission goals of universal segregation, collection, material recovery and legacy site remediation.âUntil these systems fully mature, unsegregated waste accumulates in public spaces that are vulnerable to open fires. These teams monitor and inspect biomass burning, dust pollution arising from construction and demolition activities, use of unauthorised fuels, illegal dumping of C&D waste or garbage, and C&D waste storage or dumping sites,â said a civic official.
